sections.h2: What does the Brunswick County Register of Deeds do?
sections.html:
The Brunswick County Register of Deeds is the office that files and safeguards the public land records for the county, from deeds and deeds of trust to maps and satisfactions. It also issues marriage licenses, certifies documents and administers oaths. The register is elected to a four-year term, and the office says it can record documents but cannot give legal advice or help prepare them.

The county itself dates to 1764, when it was formed from parts of Bladen and New Hanover counties. Some of the oldest items in the vault are grants, indentures and conveyances from that early period. Today the staff handles easements, restrictions and covenants, releases, powers of attorney, assumed names and UCC filings alongside the everyday deed traffic from home sales along the coast.

If you are selling a house in Brunswick County, this is the office where your deed ends up. A sale is not fully public until the new owner's deed is on the record, so the details below on format, fees and tax are worth reading before closing day.

sections.h2: Where is the Brunswick County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The office sits in Building I at 75 Courthouse Drive NE in Bolivia, NC 28422, and the main number is 910-253-2690, with an alternate toll-free line at 877-625-9310. Mail goes to PO Box 87, Bolivia, NC 28422. Hours differ by service, so check the one you need.

  • Recording: 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, Monday through Friday, except county holidays.
  • Land and vital records: 8:30 am to 5 pm, Monday through Friday.
  • Marriage licenses: 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, by appointment.
  • Passports: 8:30 am to 3:30 pm, by appointment.

Documents can be dropped off in person, mailed to the PO Box, or sent by FedEx, UPS or another courier to the Courthouse Drive street address.

sections.h2: What must a deed look like to be recorded in Brunswick County?
sections.html:
A deed has to carry original signatures, a clear notary seal and a prepared-by name and address on the first page, and it must meet the state paper and margin standards. The county posts its own checklist for what the clerks look for at the counter.

  • Payment of the recording fee, with a check payable to BCROD and a self-addressed stamped envelope for the return.
  • The names and addresses of both the grantor (seller) and the grantee (buyer) on the document.
  • Proper signatures and notarization, with a notary seal that is legible.
  • Delinquent tax certification before a deed is accepted.
  • Excise tax paid, which the county explains as $2 per $1,000 of the sales price.

On format, the county repeats the standards from G.S. 161-14(b): 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 inch paper, a three inch blank band at the top of page one, half inch margins elsewhere, black type on white paper no smaller than 9 points, one side of the page only, and the type of instrument stated below the top margin. A document that misses those standards can still be recorded, but the office adds a $25 charge for a non-standard instrument.

sections.h2: How much does recording cost in Brunswick County?
sections.html:
Recording charges in Brunswick County follow the uniform fees set by state law, plus the county's own copy prices. The table below pulls the figures the way the official pages print them.

Brunswick County and North Carolina recording charges for a deed sale
ItemCharge as printedSource
Recording a general instrument$26.00 for the first 15 pages, then $4.00 per added pageG.S. 161-10
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 for the first 35 pages, then $4.00 per added pageG.S. 161-10
Satisfaction or cancellationNo feeBrunswick County recording page
Non-standard document$25.00 addedBrunswick County recording page
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each added pageBrunswick County real estate records page
Uncertified copy25 cents per page, plus $1.00 or a stamped envelope by mailBrunswick County real estate records page
Excise tax on a conveyance$1.00 per $500Brunswick County real estate records page

Maps and plats have their own schedule. The state fee sheet lists plats at $21.00 per sheet, and a plat in this county must be 18 by 24 inches on film or mylar and pass review by the county review officer under G.S. 47-30.2.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax when a Brunswick County house sells?
sections.html:
The seller pays it. State law makes the transferor responsible for paying the tax to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded, and the rate is one dollar for each $500 of the price or fraction of it.

The county's records page notes that the rate has changed over the decades and lists older rates of $0.50 and $0.55 per $500 for earlier periods, which explains why very old deeds carry different stamps. For a current sale, ask the closing attorney to show the tax line on your settlement statement. Half of what the county collects stays in its general fund, and the other half goes to the state Department of Revenue.

Back taxes matter here too. The county lists tax certification as a condition of recording a deed, and electronic deeds must say that delinquent taxes will be paid by the closing attorney to the county tax collector when proceeds are disbursed. If you are selling with taxes owed, ask the tax collector for a payoff figure before the closing date.

sections.h2: Can lenders and title companies e-record in Brunswick County?
sections.html:
Yes, businesses and lending institutions can e-record through a vendor called Inttek, during the same 8:30 am to 4:30 pm weekday window used for counter recording. Individual homeowners generally record on paper, in person or by mail.

  • Credit card and PayPal payments carry a vendor fee of 6% of the total cost of the document plus $0.50.
  • ACH transfers into escrow carry a fee of 2.5% of the amount placed into escrow.
  • Regular recording fees still apply on top of the vendor charge.
  • Maps can now be e-recorded, but only for an existing parcel.

Every e-recorded deed needs a prepared-by statement naming a North Carolina attorney and the delinquent tax language, plus a submitter statement that cites the submitter agreement with the county. If your closing is handled by a title firm, ask whether it records electronically, since that is usually how the deed reaches the office the same day.

sections.h2: How do I look up a deed or get a copy in Brunswick County?
sections.html:
Use the county's online record search, which covers recordings from September 1939 to the present and lets you search by grantor, grantee, document type, date range or book and page. One search field is enough, and typing your name in the buyer field is the quickest way to find your own deed. Each result has a download PDF link.

Older index books for 1932 through 1953 are scanned as legacy indexes, where you find the name alphabetically and then enter the book and page. For a certified copy, mail a written request and payment to BCROD, or request it through the search site. Anyone can also ask the office to remove a Social Security, bank or card number from an image posted online, using the redaction request form.

The register also runs a free fraud alert service that notifies you when a document is recorded in your name, and the office publishes guidance on deed fraud for owners, agents and closing attorneys. It costs nothing and suits owners of vacant or inherited property.

sections.h2: What does Brunswick County look like in Census figures?
sections.html:
Brunswick County had an estimated 174,702 residents on July 1, 2025, up 27.8% from the 2020 base, and the Census Bureau counts 116,023 housing units. About 36.6% of residents are 65 or older, which is a much older profile than most of the state.

Owners occupy 84.6% of homes in the 2020 to 2024 survey, and the median value of an owner-occupied home is $349,800. Median household income is $77,024, median gross rent is $1,351 and the county issued 4,457 building permits in 2025. Land area is 850.08 square miles. Rapid growth, a high owner share and a high median value mean a steady flow of deeds through the Bolivia office.

Source for these figures: Census QuickFacts for Brunswick County.

sections.h2: Why does recording matter if I am selling a Brunswick County house?
sections.html:
Recording fixes the order of claims on the land. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance is not valid against lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies, and priority follows the time of registration.

That is why the buyer's attorney will not release funds until the deed and any deed of trust are filed. For a seller, it also means your old mortgage should show a recorded satisfaction. The bank is responsible for filing it and the county charges nothing, so ask the lender for confirmation after payoff.

If the house has been inherited, has liens or has unpaid taxes, the recording steps take longer, and it helps to sort out the title questions with the closing attorney early. A written offer from a cash buyer still needs the same deed, the same tax certification and the same excise payment.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Brunswick County?
faqs.a: At the Register of Deeds in Building I, 75 Courthouse Drive NE, Bolivia, NC 28422, or by mail to PO Box 87. Recording hours are 8:30 am to 4:30 pm on weekdays, except holidays, and the main number is 910-253-2690.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a Brunswick County deed?
faqs.a: The excise tax is $1.00 per $500 of the price or value conveyed. The county explains it on its recording page as $2 per $1,000, and the seller pays it to the register before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed of trust in Brunswick County?
faqs.a: State law sets a deed of trust or mortgage at $64.00 for the first 35 pages plus $4.00 for each additional page. A satisfaction of a paid-off mortgage is recorded with no charge.

faqs.q: Can I e-record a deed myself in Brunswick County?
faqs.a: E-recording is offered to businesses and lending institutions through Inttek, not to private owners. It adds a vendor fee of 6% plus $0.50 on card payments or 2.5% on ACH escrow transfers, and the usual recording fees still apply.

faqs.q: How do I get a certified copy of my Brunswick County deed?
faqs.a: Mail a written request with payment to BCROD, PO Box 87, Bolivia, NC 28422, or order from the online search results. A certified copy is $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each added page.
